q7.answer: The document says workers read the new billing_mode and act on it, but it does not say whether they poll or are notified, and it says nothing about an invoice that is mid-processing when the mode changes. Those two points were never decided.

q8.answer: The controller checks the gate before it writes billing_mode with compare-and-set, and that check is what stops a premature promotion. Where the gate evidence lives is only a proposal (the config service, next to billing_mode), and open question 5 leaves it unresolved.

q9.answer: The trigger is a charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute sliding window, measured for the new engine in both or new_only (before day 35 only in new_only), and it starts the rollback. The document never names the component that watches this rate or runs the check.

q10.answer: Once the freeze is confirmed, the new engine makes no new charges, and the old engine charges nothing until billing_mode is set to old_only. After that, its catch-up step charges only invoices that are due and have no ledger charge. The document does not specify how long a due charge can wait in that gap.

q11.answer: The design relies on one charge per invoice ID: a unique constraint in the ledger and the same ID sent to the provider as its idempotency key, used by both engines, so a second charge is blocked at two points. The old engine also charges only invoices with no ledger charge, and in-flight charges are resolved by status query rather than retried. This double-charge protection is marked as a proposal in the document.

q12.answer: billing_mode stays at its last applied value, and the failed step is repeated safely. A half-finished rollback never moves back to both or new_only on its own, and the new-engine freeze must be confirmed before any old-engine charge runs. The document does not say who triggers the repeat.
